title: Delete Linked List Node
statement:
Delete a node from a singly linked list when you are given only that node.

Contract
- `node` is a reference to a non-tail node that is already inside a singly linked list.
- Remove that logical node by copying data from its successor and bypassing the successor. The list head is not provided and must not be needed.
- If `node` is null or `node.next` is null, throw `IllegalArgumentException` because the deletion cannot be performed under this API.
- The relative order of all other logical values must stay the same.

Examples
- In `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4`, deleting the node currently holding `2` leaves `1 -> 3 -> 4`.
- In `7 -> 8`, deleting the node holding `7` leaves `8` at that same reference.
- Deleting null or the tail node is invalid.
hints: Without the previous node, you cannot redirect a pointer that points to `node`.
Instead, copy the next node value into `node`, then skip over the next node.
This works only when a successor exists. Intended complexity: O(1) for one deletion; the probe measures many independent deletions.
inputSyntax: Input: list values followed by the zero-based node index to delete, for example: [1, 2, 3, 4] 1
